headline: KU students lock admin building, boycott classes over hidden camera allegation
summary: Students at Khulna University have launched a protest after a mobile phone was allegedly found hidden in a washroom, sparking fears over privacy and security.
details: Students of Khulna University (KU) have locked the university's administrative building and boycotted classes to protest against the discovery of a hidden camera in a washroom.
The unrest began after a mobile phone was allegedly found hidden in a washroom, leading to students to believe it was being used as a hidden camera for illicit recording.
Protesting students are demanding a thorough investigation into the incident and strict action against those responsible for placing the device.
The campus atmosphere remains tense as students continue their boycott of academic activities to ensure their privacy and security concerns are addressed.
caption:
A hidden camera in a washroom? KU students are taking a stand against privacy breaches.

Students of Khulna University (KU) have locked the university's administrative building and boycotted classes to protest against the discovery of a hidden camera in a washroom.

The unrest began after a mobile phone was allegedly found hidden in a washroom, leading to students to believe it was being used as a hidden camera for illicit recording.

Protesting students are demanding a thorough investigation into the incident and strict action against those responsible for placing the device.

The campus atmosphere remains tense as students continue their boycott of academic activities to ensure their privacy and security concerns are addressed.

headline: Ctg Board HSC exams to resume July 27 after flood suspension
summary: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon confirms the exams will follow the original routine, with registration for missed tests starting soon.
details: Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations under the Chattogram Education Board will resume on July 27, according to Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon.
The exams had been suspended indefinitely on July 16 due to severe flooding across several districts, which caused damaged roads and transport disruptions.
The board had cited concerns over candidates' safety and wellbeing as the primary reason for the indefinite suspension.
Education Minister Milon stated that registration will now begin for candidates who were unable to sit for the examinations held on July 13 because of the flooding.
According to the existing routine, written examinations are scheduled to continue until August 8, and practical examinations are expected to conclude by mid-August.
caption:
HSC exams in Chattogram are back on track! 📚

After being suspended due to severe flooding, the board has set a new date.

Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations under the Chattogram Education Board will resume on July 27, according to Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon.

The exams had been suspended indefinitely on July 16 due to severe flooding across several districts, which caused damaged roads and transport disruptions.

The board had cited concerns over candidates' safety and wellbeing as the primary reason for the indefinite suspension.

Education Minister Milon stated that registration will now begin for candidates who were unable to sit for the examinations held on July 13 because of the flooding.

According to the existing routine, written examinations are scheduled to continue until August 8, and practical examinations are expected to conclude by mid-August.
